overview: Computer systems analysts connect business needs with technology. They study how an organization uses its computer systems, design improvements, test and maintain programs and help staff solve technical problems. O*NET rates knowledge of computers and electronics at 4.63 out of 5 for this job and speaking at 4. Education paths vary: 51% report an associate degree and 42% a bachelor's degree in O*NET data. The BLS May 2025 median is $105,850 across 519,530 jobs, making it one of the largest tech careers. The work is office-based with regular hours and occasional tight deadlines.
pay: Computer systems analysts earn a median of $105,850, and the top 10% earn $167,710 or more. Rhode Island has the highest state median at $134,630, 27% above the national figure, followed by Washington and Massachusetts. California has the most jobs by far, 59,060, at a median of $127,720.

faq.q: How much do computer systems analysts make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $105,850 a year. The middle half earn between $82,860 and $134,110. Rhode Island, Washington ($129,410) and Massachusetts ($128,240) pay the most, while Arkansas and Idaho have the lowest state medians, at $81,760 and $75,310.

faq.q: What degree do you need to be a computer systems analyst?
faq.a: Many employers prefer a bachelor's degree in computer science or information technology, but it is not the only path. In O*NET data, 51% of systems analysts report an associate degree and 42% a bachelor's degree. There are 4 related majors, including information technology.

faq.q: What does a computer systems analyst do?
faq.a: A systems analyst finds out what users need, designs or adjusts systems to fit, then tests and troubleshoots them. O*NET rates speaking at 4 out of 5 and reading comprehension at 3.88, because much of the job is explaining technical choices to managers and staff.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to computer systems analyst?
faq.a: Computer and Information Systems Managers are an 82% match and earn $175,140, 65% more. Data Scientists are a 76% match and earn $120,230, 14% more, according to BLS May 2025 data. Business Intelligence Analysts are an 81% match for moving into this job.
